question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 3 & 35 \\ 3 & -2 & 85\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 3 & 35 \\ 3 & -2 & 85\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{35}{2} \\ 3 & -2 & 85\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{35}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{13}{2} & \frac{65}{2}\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{13}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{35}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -5\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & -6 & 50 \\ 2 & -3 & 15\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & -6 & 50 \\ 2 & -3 & 15\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & \frac{50}{3} \\ 2 & -3 & 15\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & \frac{50}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{55}{3}\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=\frac{50}{3} \\ y &=-\frac{55}{3}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-\frac{55}{3}$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2\left(-\frac{55}{3}\right)=\frac{50}{3}\,\Rightarrow\,x=\frac{50}{3}-\frac{110}{3}=-20.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-20$ and $y=-\frac{55}{3}.$
